interim_updates.note_text: AEL Group revenue more than doubled YoY, up 114.5% to Rs 16.59bn for Q1 FY2026/27 (three months ended 30 June 2026), driven overwhelmingly by two segments: the Automobile segment (importing/distribution of vehicles) grew revenue from Rs 2.26bn to Rs 8.06bn (+256%), contributing Rs 5.80bn of the Rs 8.85bn total revenue increase (about 65% of the increase), while the Condominium Properties segment recognised Rs 2.57bn of revenue in this quarter versus zero in the prior-year comparative (unit handovers), contributing a further Rs 2.57bn (about 29% of the increase). Civil Engineering, the largest legacy segment, grew a more modest 12.7% (Rs 3.15bn to Rs 3.55bn). Group operating profit grew 105% to Rs 3.76bn, roughly in line with revenue, and segment operating profit shows Automobile (+391% to Rs 1.16bn) and Condominium Properties (+3,886% to Rs 867mn, from a low base of Rs 21.7mn) as the largest contributors, while Construction Material Production operating profit fell 29% (Rs 337mn to Rs 240mn). Below the operating line, Group finance costs rose 167% YoY to Rs 1.40bn (from Rs 523mn), driven mainly by the Civil Engineering segment (finance cost swung from Rs 207mn to Rs 598mn) and the Condominium Properties segment (Rs 79mn to Rs 424mn), reflecting higher borrowings used to fund construction/property inventory and the vehicle import pipeline; this was more than offset by a 1,349% jump in finance income (Rs 10mn to Rs 150mn) and a 30% increase in share of equity-accounted investee profit (ZPMC Lanka and Blue Star Realties, Rs 39mn to Rs 51mn), so Group PBT still grew 88.7% to Rs 2.57bn and PAT grew 91.5% to Rs 1.88bn. Non-controlling interest's share of profit rose sharply (Rs 19mn to Rs 167mn) as the Automobile and Condominium segments (which carry minority stakes) drove most of the growth, so profit attributable to equity holders of the parent grew a slower but still strong 77.9% (Rs 963mn to Rs 1.71bn), and basic EPS rose 78.1% (Rs 0.96 to Rs 1.71). At the standalone Company level the picture is very different: Company revenue grew just 1% and PBT actually fell 19.4% (Rs 651mn to Rs 525mn) as Company finance costs nearly doubled (+94% to Rs 678mn, debt-to-equity up from 90% to 99%) while Company operating profit grew a more modest 20.1% -- the growth story here is concentrated in subsidiaries (Automobile, Condominium Properties), not the parent's own civil engineering operations.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: no quarter closer to this one has been collected for AEL -- this is the first financial_statements entry for this symbol. YoY comparison uses the filing's own prior-year comparative column (three months ended 30 June 2025). The filing's own balance-sheet comparative is versus 31 March 2026 (FYE, audited), not 30 June 2025, consistent with standard interim SOFP presentation -- this is NOT used for any QoQ purpose, only as the filing's own point-in-time comparative.
interim_updates.takeaway: Group revenue and profit growth look spectacular (+115% revenue, +91% PAT) but are driven almost entirely by two segments -- Automobile (+256% revenue) and Condominium Properties (handovers of Rs 2.57bn from a zero base) -- not by the core Civil Engineering construction business (+12.7%). At the standalone parent Company level, PBT actually fell 19% YoY as finance costs nearly doubled, so the headline consolidated growth largely reflects subsidiary-level (and partly non-controlling-interest) performance rather than a broad-based improvement in the parent's own operations.
operational_highlights: Group revenue +114.5% YoY to Rs 16.59bn; Group PAT +91.5% YoY to Rs 1.88bn; basic EPS +78.1% to Rs 1.71
Automobile segment revenue +256% YoY to Rs 8.06bn, ~65% of the total revenue increase; segment operating profit +391% to Rs 1.16bn
Condominium Properties segment recognised Rs 2.57bn revenue this quarter vs nil in Q1 FY2025/26 (unit handovers); segment operating profit rose from Rs 21.7mn to Rs 867mn
Group finance costs +167% YoY to Rs 1.40bn, driven by Civil Engineering (Rs 207mn to Rs 598mn) and Condominium Properties (Rs 79mn to Rs 424mn) segments
Group finance income +1,349% YoY (Rs 10mn to Rs 150mn); share of equity-accounted investees (ZPMC Lanka, Blue Star Realties) +30% to Rs 51mn
Company (standalone) PBT fell 19.4% YoY to Rs 525mn as Company finance costs rose 94% to Rs 678mn; debt-to-equity ratio rose from 90% to 99%
key_drivers: Automobile segment (vehicle importing/distribution) is the single largest driver of Group revenue growth: +256% YoY to Rs 8.06bn, ~65% of the total Rs 8.85bn revenue increase
Condominium Properties segment handovers contributed Rs 2.57bn of revenue this quarter against zero in the prior-year comparative, ~29% of the total revenue increase

Group finance costs nearly tripled in the Civil Engineering segment (Rs 207mn to Rs 598mn) and Condominium Properties segment (Rs 79mn to Rs 424mn), reflecting higher borrowings to fund construction inventory, property WIP and vehicle imports
Non-controlling interest absorbed a growing share of profit (Rs 19mn to Rs 167mn, +778%) as the fastest-growing segments (Automobile, Condominium Properties) carry minority stakes
